Execution under a service identity always has administrator rights across the whole organization, so its access needs no review
User-scoped execution ignores markings, because the invoking users are already authenticated when they call the Function

stem: An application's automation started failing at 03:00 and users noticed at 09:00. The team wants to detect this kind of failure within minutes in future. What should be set up?

choices.text: Alerts on failed and missing runs, routed to the owning team's rotation, with a runbook
Ask users to report problems as soon as they arrive at work in the morning
A weekly review meeting where the whole team looks through the automation's run history together on a shared screen
Restart the automation every night at 02:55 to prevent failures at 03:00

stem: An application team wants all members to be able to merge changes to production Actions instantly to move faster. A security reviewer objects. What is a balanced approach?

choices.text: Branch protection with required review, kept fast with small changes and quick branch builds
Allow merges only once a quarter in a large release
Let everyone merge directly to production, since speed is more important than review for internal applications
Freeze all changes to production Actions permanently so that nothing can go wrong

stem: A module is shared with a partner organization's users, who should see only partner-related objects. Internal users see everything. How should access be designed?

choices.text: Copy the partner objects into a separate dataset each night and email it to the partner
Give the partner's users the module and data-level controls limiting them to partner objects
Share the module with the partner organization and rely on the module's filters to hide internal objects from them
Give partner users accounts in the internal organization so that they can see everything internal users see

stem: A function-backed Action runs project-scoped under a service identity. After a security review, the identity's permissions were reduced, and now the Action fails for everyone. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Switch the Action to run as an administrator account
Restore the identity's original broad permissions immediately so that the Action works again
Identify exactly what the Action reads and writes, grant only that to the identity, and test
Delete the Action and ask users to edit objects directly

stem: Users report that an AI-assisted application has become slow and occasionally returns errors since yesterday. The application uses Ontology queries, a Function and an AIP Logic call. How should the developer locate the cause efficiently?

choices.text: Ask users to retry their requests until they succeed
Switch the AIP Logic call to a larger model, since AI is usually the slowest part
Rewrite all three components in parallel, assuming they are all responsible for the slowdown
Use per-component monitoring and traces to find which step's latency or errors changed

stem: A Facility object type is keyed on the facility's street address. When a facility's address was corrected in the source, its maintenance history and user comments disappeared from the application. What is the cause and the fix?

choices.text: The application's cache kept the old address, so users should clear their browsers and the history will reappear for that facility
Address corrections are not supported by the Ontology, so the source team should stop correcting addresses
The key changed with the address, creating a new object; switch to a stable facility id and migrate edits and links
The maintenance history was deleted by the correction in the source, so it must be re-entered manually by the technicians

stem: An insurance application models Policies, and each policy can have many Coverages of different types with different properties (auto coverage has vehicle fields, home coverage has property fields). How should coverages be modelled?

choices.text: One Coverage object type with every possible field for every coverage kind, most of them empty for any given coverage
One object type per policy, with coverage fields added as new properties each time a policy adds a coverage
Coverage details stored as one long JSON text property on the Policy object, parsed by each application
Separate object types per coverage kind implementing a common Coverage interface, each linked to its Policy

stem: A team designs a returns workflow. One proposal puts all logic (eligibility, refund calculation, warehouse notification, customer email) into a single Workshop button script. Another separates them into components. Which design is better and why?

choices.text: Separate components: a Function for eligibility and refund, an Action for the return, and automations for notifications
The single button script, since one place for all logic is easier to read than several components working together
Skip automation and ask the warehouse to check a list of returns every afternoon
Put everything into an AIP Logic prompt so that the model handles eligibility, calculation and notifications flexibly

stem: An auditor asks which applications and automations can change Contract objects, and which Actions they use. What is the most efficient way to answer?

choices.text: Interview every application owner and compile their answers into a spreadsheet over several weeks
Use Workflow Lineage on Contract to list its Actions and the modules and automations using them
Tell the auditor that this information cannot be determined
Search the codebase for the word "contract" and assume every match changes Contract objects

stem: Which link cardinality correctly models "each Ticket is assigned to at most one Agent at a time, and an Agent handles many Tickets"?

choices.text: Many-to-one from Ticket to Agent, backed by an agent id on the ticket
One-to-one between Ticket and Agent, since a ticket has exactly one agent
Many-to-many between Ticket and Agent, since agents and tickets are both numerous
No link; store the agent's name as text on the ticket

stem: A hospital wants an application where nurses record vital signs, and a doctor is alerted when readings cross thresholds. Nurses work on tablets; doctors receive alerts on their phones. Which assembly fits?

choices.text: A single desktop module that nurses must walk to a workstation to use
An AI agent that reads all vitals continuously and decides on its own whether to call a doctor
A tablet Record Vitals Action, a threshold automation, and a notification to the doctor
A spreadsheet that nurses update and doctors check every hour on their phones

stem: Two teams created separate "Customer" object types for their applications. Reports now disagree on customer counts, and links from Orders point to one type or the other. What should be done?

choices.text: Keep both object types and ask report authors to sum them, accepting some double counting
Delete one team's object type immediately, regardless of the applications that depend on it
Rename one type to "Customer2" so that the two are easier to tell apart
Consolidate on one Customer type with a stable key and migrate links, edits and apps

stem: A property used by eight applications must change its meaning (from "estimated cost" to "approved cost"). Some applications need the old meaning for six more months. What is the safest approach?

choices.text: Freeze the property forever and create no new properties, so that no application ever has to change
Add a new property for the new meaning, keep the old one during transition, migrate apps via lineage, retire the old later
Keep the property and its name but change the pipeline that fills it, so that applications receive the new meaning silently
Change the meaning in place and send an email asking the eight application owners to adapt their applications

stem: A Reassign Ticket Action lets team leads move a ticket to another agent. The business requires that the new agent belongs to the same team and is not on leave. How should this be enforced?

choices.text: A weekly report listing reassignments to agents on leave, so that managers can correct them afterwards
Submission criteria on the Action checking the target agent's team and leave status at execution, with a clear message
Show a warning text in the form reminding team leads to check the new agent's team and leave status before submitting
Remove the reassign capability and let tickets stay with their original agent indefinitely

stem: An Action's execution history shows frequent failures with a validation message that the "end date must be after start date", but users insist they entered valid dates. What should the developer investigate?

choices.text: Whether users are lying about their inputs, and add a stronger warning to the form telling them to be careful
Whether the Action should be rebuilt as a function-backed Action, which never has validation problems
Whether dates are converted unexpectedly (time zones, date-only vs timestamp, format) between form and validation
Whether the validation should be deleted, since users keep hitting it

stem: A Mark Delivered Action needs to set the status, record the delivery time, and increment the customer's delivered-orders count on a linked Customer object. Which implementation fits?

choices.text: A function-backed Action that edits the order and recomputes the linked customer's count, applied together
Three separate declarative Actions that users must run one after another for each delivered order
Ask users to update the customer's count by hand after marking each order as delivered
A declarative Action for the order and a nightly batch that recounts every customer's delivered orders from scratch

stem: Which statement about the security layers involved when a user runs an Action is correct?

choices.text: Markings do not apply to objects edited through Actions
If a user can see the Action's button in a module, every security check for running it has already passed
Action permissions are the same as project roles, so any Editor can run any Action in the project
Running an Action involves independent checks (run permission, object edit rights, markings)

stem: An Action creates a maintenance work order. After it succeeds, the external CMMS system must receive the work order. Sometimes the CMMS is down. What design handles this well?

choices.text: Make the Action fail entirely whenever the CMMS is unreachable, so that no work order exists without a CMMS copy
Ask technicians to retype every work order into the CMMS manually at the end of each day
Create the work order, then deliver it to the CMMS asynchronously with retries and visible status
Call the CMMS synchronously and, if it times out, call it again immediately until it responds

stem: A developer wants to verify that a revised Approve Action rejects invalid cases and accepts valid ones before release, including permission differences. Which test plan fits?

choices.text: Release the change to production and watch how many approvals fail or succeed during the first week of use
Ask one team lead to try the Action on a real object and report back
Test once as the developer, who has every permission, with one valid object
Branch tests with valid, invalid and edge cases, as users with and without permission

stem: An Action currently uses declarative rules. A new requirement adds a calculation of a late fee based on days overdue and the customer's tier. What is the right change?

choices.text: Move to a function-backed Action computing the fee from days overdue and tier, with tests for the rules
Remove the late fee requirement because declarative Actions cannot handle it
Keep it declarative and ask users to calculate the late fee themselves and type it into a form field
Add a nightly job that calculates late fees for every record and overwrites whatever was submitted

stem: A user can submit an Action that edits Project objects, but for one project the submission fails with a permission error while others succeed. The Action and the user's groups are unchanged. What is the most likely explanation and next step?

choices.text: The user's Action permission was revoked for that project only, which is impossible, so the error must be ignored
That project carries a control the user lacks (a marking or policy); check access on it
The Action should be granted to everyone in the organization to avoid future failures
The platform randomly rejects some submissions, so the user should retry until it works

stem: A function must update the status of all open tasks linked to a project when the project is cancelled. Projects can have up to 5,000 tasks. How should the edits be implemented safely?

choices.text: Loop over every task in the Ontology, checking each one's project link in memory, and edit the matching tasks one at a time
Query the project's linked tasks filtered to open status server-side and return bounded edits for them, tested on a large project
Edit only the first 100 tasks, since functions should never edit more than 100 objects in any situation
Ask users to open each task and change its status manually after cancelling the project

stem: A function that calculates shipping costs returns different results for the same inputs on different runs. The code reads the current exchange rate inside the function. What explains this and what should change?

choices.text: Rounding errors always cause different results, so round everything to whole numbers
The platform caches functions randomly, so results vary; publish a new version to clear the cache
The function is nondeterministic because TypeScript has random behaviour in arithmetic, so it should be rewritten in Python
The exchange rate changes between runs; pass it in or record the rate and timestamp used, so results are reproducible

stem: Which function requirement is the clearest case for AIP Logic rather than TypeScript or Python code?

choices.text: Checking whether an order date falls on a weekend
Sorting a list of suppliers by on-time delivery rate
Writing a readable explanation of why a claim was flagged, from flag data and notes
Summing the line items of an invoice and returning the total amount including tax for display in the application

stem: A function used by a Workshop module and an external OSDK app needs a new optional parameter. How should it be introduced without breaking either consumer?

choices.text: Publish a new version with the parameter optional and defaulted, and regenerate the OSDK
Add the parameter as required in place, since both consumers will be updated eventually by their owners
Create a second function with a different name and maintain both independently forever
Change the parameter list in the existing published version without telling the consumers

stem: A function aggregates order totals by region, but the totals are slightly lower than finance's figures. Investigation shows the function counts only the first page of results from a query. What should be fixed?

choices.text: Ask finance to adjust their figures to match the function's output
Aggregate server-side (or iterate every page) and add a test against a known total
Increase the page size to a very large number so that one page always contains all of the orders for every region
Multiply the result by a correction factor that makes it match finance's figures

stem: Before publishing a function that applies discounts, the team wants tests that will catch mistakes in edge cases. Which test set is most valuable?

choices.text: Tests that only check whether the function compiles successfully without errors
Tests generated by asking the function to test itself
One test with a typical order and a typical discount, since edge cases rarely happen in real usage
Cases for zero-value orders, maximum discounts, missing tiers, expired promotions and rounding

stem: Which statement about provenance for function-backed Actions is most accurate?

choices.text: Recording which function version and inputs produced an edit lets auditors reproduce and explain it later
Provenance is only needed for AIP Logic functions, never for TypeScript or Python functions
Provenance means storing the function's source code inside every edited object as a text property
Provenance is irrelevant because Actions already record who ran them, so the function's logic version never matters

stem: A function written in Python by a former data scientist is now maintained by application developers who work only in TypeScript, and it contains simple deterministic logic. It fails occasionally and nobody wants to touch it. What should be considered?

choices.text: Delete it and ask consumers to implement the logic themselves
Convert it to AIP Logic so that the model can handle its occasional failures automatically
Rewrite it in TypeScript v2 with equivalence tests, then switch consumers to the new version
Leave it unchanged forever, since rewriting working code is always riskier than maintaining it

stem: A module must let users filter a list of incidents by region, severity and date range, and a chart and a table must both reflect the same filters. How should the filters be wired?

choices.text: Let users export the list to a spreadsheet and filter it there before looking at the chart
Duplicate the module into one version per region, with severity and date filters fixed in each copy
Configure separate filters inside the chart and inside the table, and ask users to set them identically each time
Define shared filter variables applied to one object set variable that feeds both the chart and the table

stem: A Workshop page with ten widgets loads in 15 seconds. Profiling shows each widget makes its own heavy query for the same base object set, and two function-backed variables run on load although they are only used in a collapsed section. What should be changed?

choices.text: Share one base object set across widgets and lazy-load the collapsed section's variables
Ask users to keep the module open all day so they only pay the load time once
Add a progress bar so users understand why the page takes 15 seconds, without changing the queries
Split the page into ten pages, one per widget, so that each loads separately

stem: A module needs a button that runs an AI summary for the selected case and stores it so colleagues can see it later. How should this be connected?

choices.text: A button that calls the AI function and displays the summary in a text widget only for the current user's session
A function-backed Action calling the AI function and storing the summary with author and time
Ask users to copy the summary into an email to their colleagues
Generate the summary in the user's browser and save it to the user's local disk

stem: Which change to a widely embedded Workshop module is backward compatible?

choices.text: Removing an input variable that some of the parent modules currently set when they embed the module
Changing an output variable from an object to a list of objects
Adding a new optional input variable whose default preserves current behaviour
Renaming an existing output variable that parent modules read

stem: Users of a module complain that after they submit an Action, the page freezes for 30 seconds while a follow-up calculation runs. What is the best design change?

choices.text: Ask users to submit the Action only at the end of the day
Move the calculation to a background automation and show its status in the module
Keep the calculation synchronous and add a message asking users to wait patiently
Remove the calculation entirely, even though downstream users rely on its results

stem: A section of a module is supposed to appear only when the selected order is "On Hold", but it never appears even for on-hold orders. Other widgets show the order correctly. What should be checked?

choices.text: Whether the module must be republished for each order separately
Whether conditional visibility only works for the first hundred orders in an object set
Whether the browser blocks conditional sections for security reasons on certain devices
The visibility condition's variable and its exact compared value (case, code versus label)

stem: A module could compute a "days until due" value either with a function-backed variable or by reading a property materialized nightly by a pipeline. The value is displayed and used to sort a list of 20,000 items. Which is better?

choices.text: Hard-code the value into the module once a month
A function-backed variable recomputed for all 20,000 items on every page load, since it is always exact to the second
A nightly-materialized property for sorting, with exact values computed only for a selected item
Ask users to compute the value mentally from the due date column

stem: A Workshop application will be used by internal staff and also embedded in a partner-facing portal where partners should see a reduced set of pages and no internal Actions. What deployment approach fits?

choices.text: A partner module reusing shared components, exposing only partner pages and Actions, with data-level permissions
Give partners internal accounts so they can use the full internal module
Embed the same internal module in the partner portal and hide internal pages with CSS so partners cannot see them
Email partners screenshots of the relevant pages each week

stem: A team plans a customer-facing mobile app that reads order status and lets customers request changes. They debate building it on the OSDK versus embedding a Workshop module. Customers have no Foundry accounts. Which choice fits better?

choices.text: Publish the order dataset publicly so that the mobile app can read it without any authentication at all
Embed the internal Workshop module directly in the mobile app and give every customer a Foundry account to sign in with
An OSDK app with a backend using scoped service authentication and per-customer filtering
Email customers a daily PDF of their order status and ask them to reply with any change requests they have

stem: An external reporting tool calls Foundry's REST API to list Ticket objects modified in the last hour, every five minutes. The response sometimes misses tickets. What is a likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The tool should call the API once per second instead of every five minutes to catch more tickets
The tool reads only the first page of results; follow page tokens until the result set is exhausted on each call
Tickets modified in the last hour are not available through the API until the next day
The REST API randomly drops objects from responses, so the tool should call it twice and merge the results each time

choices.text: Rotate the secret, move secret-based calls server-side (or use user OAuth), and minimize scope
Share the secret with the security team so that they can monitor its use
Obfuscate the secret in the JavaScript bundle so that it is harder to read for curious users
Keep the secret in the bundle but restrict the app to the corporate network, which makes any exposure of it impossible

stem: An OSDK application deployed last month suddenly receives errors after a teammate narrowed the application's scopes in the developer console. Reads of Orders still work, but listing Shipments fails. What happened?

choices.text: The OSDK package has expired and must be renewed each month
The Shipment object type was deleted from the Ontology at the same time as the scope change by coincidence
The users' permissions on Shipments were removed by the scope change
Shipments are no longer in the app's scope, so access fails regardless of user permissions; restore it if needed

stem: Which approach is best for an external app that must show, for each of 2,000 customers, their number of open tickets?

choices.text: Ask support staff to maintain a manual list of open ticket counts
Download every ticket nightly into the app's own database and count there
For each customer, fetch all their tickets and count them in the app, making 2,000 sequential requests
One aggregation request grouping open tickets by customer and returning counts

stem: An application team adds new features every week that need additional object types. They want to avoid failures caused by forgetting to update the OSDK. What practice helps?

choices.text: Grant the application scope to all object types in the Ontology once, so that regeneration is never needed again
Put scope updates and OSDK regeneration in the release checklist and CI
Stop using the OSDK and send raw HTTP requests without types
Hand-edit generated SDK files whenever a new type is needed, to avoid waiting for regeneration

Increase the spinner's animation speed so that users perceive the application as faster while they wait for Foundry
Ask users to refresh the page whenever the spinner appears
Hide all errors so that users never see technical messages

stem: An internal analytics app currently uses one service identity for all users, so everyone sees all data. Auditors require that each user sees only what their permissions allow. What change is needed?

choices.text: Give every user administrator rights so that the service identity is no longer needed
Ask users not to look at data outside their department

Keep the service identity and add a filter in the app's code that hides data based on the user's department name

choices.text: A trigger on any change to any property of any shipment that emails the customer whenever something changes
A daily schedule that emails every customer with any delayed shipment, every day, for as long as the shipment stays delayed
A trigger on object creation, since every shipment is created before it can become delayed

choices.text: Make an administrator the automation's owner so that it never fails, and trust the summary content to be safe
Remove the automation and ask analysts to post summaries manually
Switch the automation to project-scoped mode, which on its own prevents it from reading anything outside the project
Make the owner a service user with access only to what the summaries need, since effects run as the owner

stem: An automation that applies a discount when an order total exceeds 1,000 occasionally applies the discount twice. Logs show it ran twice when two line items were added to the order within the same second. What is happening and how is it fixed?

The order total is calculated incorrectly, so the threshold should be raised to 2,000
Users should be prevented from adding more than one line item per minute
The platform has a bug that duplicates runs at random, and nothing at all can be done in the automation's own design

stem: An automation's evaluation history shows its condition is evaluated on every update, but the effect never runs. The condition compares a status to "approved". Objects do show status "Approved" in the application. What is the likely cause?

choices.text: The automation only runs its effects on weekdays, and all of the recent updates happened to occur at the weekend
The objects are too large for automations to evaluate
The stored value differs in case or code from "approved"; compare it and fix the condition
The automation's effect is disabled by the platform after 100 evaluations

stem: A team needs to remind account managers about contracts expiring in 30 days. Expiry dates are stored on Contract objects. Which automation design fits?

A trigger on contract creation that waits 30 days less than the contract term inside the effect before sending a reminder
A daily scheduled automation querying contracts expiring in exactly 30 days and notifying their managers idempotently

stem: An automation's notifications are going to a team channel, but the team says they are overwhelmed by hundreds of low-value alerts and ignore them. Real failures are missed. What should change?

choices.text: Send only actionable failures to the team, put warnings in a digest, and tune conditions
Send the notifications to more channels as well, so that someone somewhere notices the important ones among the hundreds
Turn off all notifications, since the team ignores them anyway
Ask the team to read every notification carefully

stem: An automation posts invoices to an ERP when they are approved. Occasionally the ERP accepts the invoice but the automation's response times out, and it retries. How should duplicates be prevented?

choices.text: Disable retries so that a timeout never leads to a second attempt, even when the first attempt really failed
Wait 24 hours before retrying any failed attempt
Send an idempotency key per invoice and store the ERP reference once confirmed
Ask the ERP team to delete duplicate invoices every morning

stem: Before enabling a new automation that will change thousands of objects nightly, the team wants confidence in its behaviour and a way to stop it quickly if something goes wrong. What should be in place?

choices.text: Enable it on all objects immediately and review the results the next morning
Test on representative objects, start with a small subset, monitor, and keep a mute switch
Skip testing entirely because the automation only uses existing Actions that have already been tested on their own
Ask users to report any unexpected changes they notice

stem: An application lets HR staff ask an AI assistant questions about company policies, answered from the policy documents in the Ontology. Staff must be able to check where each answer came from. How should the assistant be configured?

choices.text: Retrieve relevant policy chunks, answer only from them, and return citations to the source sections in a typed output
Paste every policy document into each prompt so that the model always has complete information available
Answer from the model's general knowledge of employment law, since most company policies follow common practice
Return the full text of the most relevant policy document instead of an answer

stem: A product owner wants an AI agent that can both answer questions about orders and cancel, refund or reship them on request, all automatically. What design reflects the guide's principles?

choices.text: Remove all write capabilities and let the agent only answer questions, forever

Let the agent prepare changes for user confirmation through validated Actions with limits
Let the agent run Actions as an administrator so it never fails on permissions

stem: An AI classification feature in an application was accurate last month but now mislabels many items. No prompt change was made. Traces show inputs now contain a new product category the prompt does not mention. What should the developer do?

Update the prompt's categories and examples, add cases for the new category, and re-run the suite
Increase the temperature so that the model becomes more creative about handling categories it has not seen before
Remove the classification feature since it is no longer reliable

stem: AI FDE generated a TypeScript Function that loads Customer objects, calls an LLM for each, and writes a "churn reason" property. A reviewer must decide what to check before publishing. Which check is most important for platform idioms?

That the Function is written in as few lines as possible
That the LLM's responses are long and detailed for each customer
That it queries a bounded, filtered object set and writes edits through the governed mechanism

stem: Which is the best use of an AI-backed Action in an application?

choices.text: An Action that uses AI to calculate the sum of an invoice's line items
An Action that uses AI to validate that a date field is in the correct format
AI drafting a customer reply that the agent edits before the Action sends it
An Action that uses AI to decide whether a user has permission to approve a payment

stem: An AI feature needs a customer's name, open tickets and contract tier to draft a renewal email. The developer currently passes the entire Customer object including payment details and internal risk notes. What should change?

Pass nothing and ask the model to invent a generic renewal email

stem: Users can thumbs-up or thumbs-down AI summaries in an application. The team wants this feedback to improve the feature. What should they do with it?

choices.text: Link feedback to traces, review negatives, and turn verified failures into evaluation cases
Count thumbs-down per week and report the number to management without examining any examples
Automatically retrain the foundation model on the feedback
Ignore feedback because users are subjective

stem: A team relies heavily on AI FDE to produce Functions and wants to speed up releases by skipping human review when generated code passes automated tests. What is the guide-aligned position?

choices.text: Let AI FDE review its own code and publish if it reports no issues
Keep focused human review of schema, idioms and side effects, automating mechanical checks
Skip human review whenever automated tests pass, since generated code that passes tests is always safe
Ban AI FDE entirely, since generated code can never be trusted

stem: A claims application must let adjusters in each region see only their region's claims, while supervisors see all regions. Claims are Ontology objects. Which control should be used?

choices.text: A Workshop filter defaulted to the adjuster's region, which adjusters are trusted not to change when they open the module
Separate object types per region, each duplicated from the same source, with project roles per region
An object security policy (or a restricted view backing the type) granting rows by region attribute, with supervisors seeing all
A marking per region applied to the whole claims dataset so each adjuster holds only their region's marking

stem: An executive wants a new dashboard module shared with 200 managers. The module reads several object types, some of which contain data that certain managers should not see. How should sharing be designed?

choices.text: Share the module (resource access) with the managers, and let each user's data permissions decide what they see within it
Send each manager a weekly PDF export instead of sharing the module at all
Copy all data the module needs into a single new unrestricted dataset so that sharing is simple
Give all 200 managers Owner on every project the module reads from, so that the module works for everyone without errors

stem: A Function runs project-scoped under a service identity and writes summaries to Report objects. Users report that some Reports created by it are visible to people who should not see them. What should be reviewed?

choices.text: Whether users should be told to close Reports they should not see
Whether the service identity should be deleted entirely, since project-scoped execution is never acceptable for any Function
Whether users are sharing their screens with colleagues who then see the Reports by accident
Where the Function writes and the permissions on the created objects

stem: Users report an application's Actions intermittently fail with timeouts at the end of each month. Monitoring shows Action latency spikes when a monthly batch automation runs. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Increase the timeout on every Action to ten minutes
Confirm contention in monitoring, then reschedule or throttle the batch
Ask users to avoid working in the application at the end of each month while the monthly batch automation is running
Disable all monitoring during month-end so that alerts do not fire

stem: Which control is most appropriate to ensure only reviewed changes reach a production application's Functions and Actions?

choices.text: A shared password for the production environment that only the senior developers on the team are told about
A weekly meeting where developers describe their changes verbally
Branch protection requiring approval before changes merge to production
Disabling all changes to production permanently

stem: A user can open an application and see objects, but a specific property column is blank for them while colleagues see values. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Property-level security restricts that property; check access to it separately from the object
The Ontology loses property values for new users until they have used the application for a week
The property is too long to display for this user's screen size
The user's display settings hide that column's text colour against the background

stem: An automation must create follow-up tasks in a project that the triggering users cannot access, by design. An auditor asks how this is controlled. What should the developer document?

choices.text: That the automation runs as the triggering user, which explains everything the auditor needs to know
That the developer personally checks the automation's output every week
