choices.text: Re-implement the submission criteria in the app and keep both copies in sync by hand
Fetch the objects and compare their properties against a list of rules saved in the app
Call the Action validation endpoint, which evaluates parameters and criteria and applies no edits
Submit the Action for real and then call a second Action to undo it if the check turned out poorly

stem: A browser-only app is registered as a public client. Its developer requests a token with the client credentials grant and the request is refused. What is the right way forward?

choices.text: Request additional scopes in the same call, since the refusal is caused by missing scopes
Register a confidential client and keep its secret inside the browser bundle so the grant is accepted
Ask an administrator to raise the app's rate limit so that the grant request is processed
Use the authorization code grant with PKCE, so each signed-in user receives a token

stem: A backend integration is enabled for the client credentials grant and its token requests succeed. Reading Customer objects still returns permission errors, although the developer can open the same objects in Workshop. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Give the application's service user access to the resources it reads, limited to what it needs
Send the developer's own username and password from the backend so the reads run as the developer
Give the service user the Owner role on every project so permission errors cannot occur again
Re-register the integration as a public client so that it inherits the developer's access

stem: Last night an automation's Action effect failed for 40 events because a submission criterion was misconfigured. The developer fixed the criterion this morning. How should the failed events be handled?

choices.text: Leave them, because failed events cannot be run again once their first attempt has failed
Delete the automation and recreate it so that all history is lost and starts fresh
Edit each of the 40 objects by hand to make the effect trigger a second time for it
Retry the failed events so they run with the latest configuration

stem: Managers want one notification when an invoice first becomes overdue, not a message every time an already overdue invoice is edited. Which trigger design fits?

choices.text: A condition on the invoice's status property being equal to Overdue, evaluated on any change
An object set trigger that fires when invoices are added to the overdue set
A time-based schedule that notifies for every overdue invoice at the top of each hour
An object-modified trigger on every invoice, which notifies for any edit made to it

stem: An automation has two Action effects: the first creates a Shipment, the second sets the related Order to Shipped and assumes the shipment already exists. Sometimes the Order update runs first and fails. What is the right fix?

choices.text: Combine the dependent edits into one Action, or make the second step independent of the first
Add a delay in front of the second effect so that the Shipment is more likely to exist by then
Rely on the order in which the effects were listed, since the configuration is applied in sequence
Move the Order update into a Workshop button so that people trigger it by hand each time

stem: An AIP Logic function answers customers' questions about stock for a product. Answers must reflect current stock levels, which change hourly. Which design is correct?

choices.text: Paste last week's stock export into the prompt so the model remembers the numbers
Fine-tune a model on past stock tables so that it learns the usual levels
Give the function a tool that queries stock objects for the requested product
Ask the model to estimate likely stock from the product name alone

stem: A team wants to switch an AIP Logic function to a cheaper model to cut costs. Which approach best balances savings against quality?

choices.text: Test the new model on three examples chosen by the developer and switch if they look fine
Keep the expensive model permanently because model changes are never worth testing
Run an evaluation suite on representative cases for both models and compare results
Switch for everyone and watch for complaints during the first month after release

stem: A developer asks AI FDE to run an Action that edits production objects, and the request is refused with a permission error. A colleague claims that AI FDE has its own service account with broader rights. How should the developer proceed?

choices.text: Treat the error as the developer's own, since AI FDE has no separate identity, and get access normally
Start new sessions repeatedly until AI FDE happens to pick a service identity that is permitted
Share a colleague's session so that AI FDE can borrow that person's wider permissions
Grant the AI FDE service account the Owner role on the object type so that the agent can carry on

stem: A partner company's staff use the application. Regardless of project roles, they must never be able to open the internal HR project. Which control provides that boundary?

choices.text: A note in the onboarding guide asking partner staff not to open the HR project at any time
Organization membership, which acts as a mandatory boundary alongside roles
A Viewer role on the HR project given to each partner user individually
A Workshop page that hides the link to the HR project from partner staff

stem: A nightly automation updates supplier ratings. Twice in a month it failed unnoticed for days. How should the team make failures visible?

choices.text: Add more retries so every failure is eventually hidden by a later success
Ask the owner to look at the automation's history each morning
Run the automation twice each night so that at least one of the two runs is likely to work
Add a fallback effect that notifies the owning team on failure, and review failed events

stem: An automation owned by an administrator edits objects through an Action effect when a user submits a request. Low-privilege users can now cause edits that they could not make directly. What is the correct reading?

choices.text: The administrator's role is applied to the users, which changes their rights everywhere
The platform runs every effect as the user who triggered it, so this cannot be happening
The edits run as the automation owner, so scope the owner's permissions and criteria deliberately
Automations are exempt from permissions altogether, which makes the owner's role irrelevant

stem: A field-service Ontology relates Technician and Site objects: each technician serves many sites and each site has many technicians. Dispatchers must record a certification level and a start date for every technician-site pairing and edit those values through Actions, and Workshop must show them when a user selects a link between a technician and a site. The ontology owner wants the relationship kept as a first-class Ontology resource rather than as columns duplicated on either object type. Which link design meets all of these requirements?

choices.text: A many-to-many link type backed by a join table dataset that holds the technician and site primary keys, generated from the two object types
A foreign key property for the site on Technician with a one-to-many link type, storing the certification level and start date beside that key
An Assignment object type with certification and start date, linked many-to-one to both sides, backing an object-backed link type
Array properties on Technician for site IDs, certification levels and start dates, kept aligned by position and all edited by one Action

stem: An asset team models Pump, Compressor and Valve object types, each with type-specific properties plus a shared operating status and last-inspection date. They need one Ontology edit function that flags overdue equipment of any of these types, keeps working without code changes when a Turbine type is added next year, and keeps the three types distinct. The developers prefer Python but can also write TypeScript. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Merge the three types into one Equipment object type with a kind property, and write a Python edit function that edits that single object type
Define an Equipment interface implemented by each type, and write the edit function in Python against that interface to match the team's preferred language
Write a Python edit function with three typed parameters, one per object type, and add a fourth parameter for Turbine when that type arrives next year
Define an Equipment interface with the shared properties, implement it on all three types, and write the edit function in TypeScript v2 against it

stem: A fleet Ontology has a one-to-one link type between Vehicle and Telematics Unit, backed by a unit_id foreign key on Vehicle that installers set through an Install Unit Action. Dispatch now finds one telematics unit linked to two vehicles, which corrupts location tracking. A double install must be blocked at the moment it is submitted, the foreign key link must stay, and installers must keep using the same Action. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Add a submission criterion to Install Unit that fails when the chosen unit is already linked to a vehicle, as one-to-one is not enforced
Make unit_id the primary key of the Vehicle object type, so that a unit can only ever appear on one vehicle object in the whole Ontology
Keep the link and Action as they are, and add a nightly pipeline check that reports units linked to more than one vehicle to the fleet team
Replace the foreign key with a many-to-many join table link, so each install becomes its own row that the fleet team can review and delete

stem: Every night a risk team must recompute a risk score for about 300,000 Supplier objects using an existing function-backed Action that accepts a set of suppliers. Applying the Action once to the whole set times out, the recompute must start without anyone pressing a button, and the team wants no new pipeline code to maintain. Which assembly meets these requirements with the LEAST additional build effort?

choices.text: A Workshop button that applies the Action to the full Supplier object set, pressed each evening by an analyst on the night shift before leaving
An automation with an Objects added to set condition on all Supplier objects, scheduled nightly, passing the added suppliers to the Action in one run
An automation with a scheduled Run on all objects condition on Supplier, passing the suppliers to the Action effect in batches of a set size
A new Python transform that computes the scores into a dataset each night, replacing the Action, and scheduled to rebuild the backing dataset

stem: A language model used by 14 AIP Logic functions across three Workshop applications owned by different teams has been marked deprecated. Before its sunset date the developer must move all 14 functions to a newer model, must first see which applications depend on each function, and must avoid opening and editing every Logic file one at a time. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Open each of the 14 Logic functions, change the model in every Use LLM block, and republish them one after another in order of usage
Search Data Lineage for the deprecated model, trace the datasets that feed each function, and update the pipelines producing their inputs
Bulk replace the model across all Logic functions on the enrollment from Workflow Lineage, without first reviewing which applications use them
Open the workflow in Workflow Lineage, review dependent applications on the graph, then bulk replace the model in the 14 functions

stem: When a planner applies a Release Order Action, Foundry must call a warehouse system, a transport system and a customer-messaging service, each through its own webhook. The order edit in Foundry must succeed even if any external call fails, the planner should not wait on the external systems, the calls need no particular order, and everything must be configured on the Action itself. How should the webhooks be configured?

choices.text: Configure all three as side effect webhooks, which run after the Ontology edits in no set order and do not hold back the success message
Call the three systems from a separate automation that watches released orders and applies one webhook-backed Action per system shortly after
Configure one side effect webhook whose input function returns three payloads, so that single webhook is called three times after the edit
Configure the warehouse call as a writeback webhook and the other two as side effects, so the warehouse confirms the release before the edit

stem: A Create Purchase Request Action must register the request in an ERP that returns a requisition number. The new Foundry object must store that number in the same submission, no Purchase Request may be created in Foundry if the ERP rejects the call, and the requester must see the ERP's error when that happens. How should the developer configure the Action?

choices.text: Configure the ERP call as a side effect webhook and map its output parameter into the Create object rule's requisition number property
Configure the ERP call as a writeback webhook and map its output parameter into the Create object rule's requisition number property
Configure the ERP call as a writeback webhook and leave the number empty, asking requesters to enter it through a second Action later
Configure the ERP call as a side effect webhook and add an automation that copies the returned number onto the object a few minutes later

stem: A Claims object type is backed by a dataset, and adjusters update claim status through an Update Claim Action. An integration team asks the developer to reopen the object type to Object Explorer edits, Foundry Forms and API calls for convenience. Security requires that adjusters gain no permission that lets them read more claim data than they already see through the Ontology, and the Action must keep working for them. Which configuration should the developer keep?

choices.text: Allow edits through Actions, Object Explorer, Forms and APIs, and grant adjusters Edit on the writeback dataset so their submissions succeed
Keep edits allowed only through Actions and also grant adjusters the Editor role on the project that holds the backing dataset, to be safe
Allow edits through Actions, Object Explorer, Forms and APIs, and give Edit on the writeback dataset only to the integration team's service user
Keep edits allowed only through Actions, so adjusters submitting Update Claim need no Edit permission on the writeback dataset at all

stem: An Approve Payment Action has a submission criterion "current user's group IDs do not include External Contractors" so that contractors cannot approve payments. A security review flags that a request made with a scoped token, which carries only part of a user's permissions, could pass this check. The team must keep contractors blocked, keep employees able to approve, and avoid maintaining lists of individual users. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Replace the negative check with a positive criterion that requires membership in a Payment Approvers group which excludes contractors
Replace the group check with a criterion that compares the current user ID with a static list of every employee allowed to approve
Remove the submission criterion and hide the Approve button in Workshop for members of the contractors group instead of checking it
Keep the negative group check and add a second NOT condition on the contractors' Organization, so a missing group attribute is still caught

stem: Planners edit delay minutes for flights in a Workshop table using an action-backed inline edit. The Delay Flight Action has two submission criteria: a flight may be delayed at most 20 minutes, and the total delay at an airport may not exceed 50 minutes. After a busy shift the airport's total reached 85 minutes, although every cell edit passed validation. The 50-minute cap must be enforced reliably. What explains this and what should change?

choices.text: Submission criteria are skipped for inline edits in tables, so neither rule ran; move both rules into the table widget's column validation settings
Inline edits are checked against unedited values and submitted in bulk, so the total rule cannot hold; apply the Action per flight instead
The Action's rules ran in a non-deterministic order, so the cap was checked before each edit; reorder the rules so the airport total check runs last
The total criterion compared against an aggregation refreshed nightly, so it used stale sums; enable auto-refresh on the table's object set

stem: A team needs one function that standardizes free-text part descriptions. It must be callable from a Pipeline Builder pipeline that cleans incoming supplier data and also from a Workshop module where buyers test single descriptions, and the team wants to use the Ontology SDK inside the function code. Only one implementation may be maintained. Which function language should they choose?

choices.text: TypeScript v2, which provides the Ontology SDK and a full Node.js runtime and can be queried from Workshop modules and their variables
AIP Logic, which can ask a language model to standardize the text without code and can be queried from Workshop modules and their variables
Python, which supports calls from Pipeline Builder pipelines, queries from Workshop modules and the Ontology SDK inside function code
TypeScript v1, which offers mature media handling and direct webhook calls and can be queried from Workshop modules and their variables

stem: A TypeScript v2 function-backed Action closes a Work Order and then, in the same function, counts the site's remaining open work orders with an object set filter on status and writes the count to the Site object. Users see that the stored count is always one higher than the true number right after a closure. The count must be correct within the same Action run. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Subtract the orders this function just closed from the query's count, since object set queries do not see the function's own edits
Add a short wait before the count query so the Ontology index catches up with the status edit made earlier in the same function run
Load the closed work order again by primary key and confirm its status reads Closed before running the object set count query
Move the count query ahead of the status edit, so it runs against freshly loaded data, and store that earlier result on the Site object

stem: A Reassign Case Action is backed by a function with auto upgrade enabled from minimum version 2.1.0. Version 2.3.0 now also creates an Audit Note object on every reassignment. Since that release, every submission fails, although the function's tests pass and pinning 2.1.0 makes submissions succeed again. The team wants to keep the new audit behaviour and keep auto upgrade. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Pin the Action to function version 2.1.0 and turn auto upgrade off, so that submissions succeed again while the team investigates further
Set the Action's minimum function version to 2.3.0, so the Action's provenance includes the Audit Note object type the new release edits
Grant users Edit on the Audit Note writeback dataset, since the failure comes from missing writeback permissions on the new object type
Add a Create object rule for Audit Note next to the existing function rule, so that the Action declares the new object type explicitly

stem: A Set Credit Limit Action is backed by a function maintained by a separate analytics team, which must stay the only maintainer of the scoring logic and publishes frequent minor releases. Governance requires that any change in what the Action does be approved by the Action's owners, who cannot edit that repository, and the Action must never fail because of an unreviewed release. Which configuration best meets these requirements?

choices.text: Enable auto upgrade from the current version, so compatible minor releases reach users quickly without any change to the Action itself
Enable auto upgrade and add a submission criterion limiting the Action to the credit team, so that only approved users can run it at all
Copy the function into the Action owners' own repository and publish it from there, ending the dependency on the analytics team's releases
Disable auto upgrade and pin a reviewed version, upgrading the Action's function rule only after the Action owners approve a release

stem: A Python edit function adds a tag to the tags array property of an Incident by calling append on editable_incident.tags and then returns the edits. It runs without errors in tests and through the Action, but the tag never appears on the object, while a status change made in the same function is saved. The fix must keep all existing tags. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Call append on the original Incident object passed into the function instead of the editable view, so that the change reaches the Ontology
Add the tags property to the edits parameter of the function decorator so that array changes made in place are tracked by the function
Copy the array into a new list, append the tag to that copy, and assign the copy back to the tags property of the editable incident
Assign a new list containing only the new tag to the tags property, because assignment is what records an edit on an editable object

stem: A Workshop button runs two events in order: Recompute Quote Total, which reruns a function-backed variable, then Set variable value, which copies Quote Total into a Saved Total variable used by an Action form. Users report that Saved Total often holds the previous total or a loading state. The function must remain the single source of the total. What should the builder change?

choices.text: Add a second Recompute Quote Total event after Set variable value so the copied value is refreshed once the recompute has completed
Change Saved Total to a function-backed variable that repeats the total calculation in a second function used only by the Action form
Swap the two events so Set variable value runs first and the Recompute Quote Total event runs immediately after it on the same button
Split the steps into separate user interactions, so the copy into Saved Total runs only after the Quote Total recompute has ended

stem: A capacity-planning module has a function-backed variable that runs a 20-second simulation from six input widgets. Planners adjust several inputs before they want a result, and today the simulation reruns after every single change. Each run costs compute, so the simulation must not run until a planner asks for it, but planners must be able to get a fresh result whenever they choose. Which configuration fits best?

choices.text: Replace the variable with a static variable that planners update by copying numbers from a separate simulation module after each run
Set the variable to recompute only when triggered by an event, and add a Run Simulation button that fires its Recompute event
Set the variable to compute on module load and when triggered by an event, so a default simulation is ready when planners first arrive
Keep automatic recompute but place the result in a collapsed section, so lazy loading defers the simulation until the section is opened

stem: A child Workshop module has a module interface variable Region with a static default of EMEA, and its tables filter on Region. A parent module embeds it and maps its own Region variable, which has no default, to the child's Region. In the parent, the child's tables stay empty until a user picks a region, while the child opened alone shows EMEA data. The parent's region picker must keep driving the child. What should the builder do?

choices.text: Unmap Region so the child uses its own EMEA default again, leaving the parent's region picker unconnected to the embedded child
Republish the child module, because the parent embeds the child's last saved version instead of the version that was last published
Set EMEA as the default of the parent's Region variable, because a mapped interface variable uses the parent module's definition
Add a reset Region value event to the child's load, so that the variable returns to the child's EMEA default every time it loads

stem: A dispatch module enables auto-refresh on a watched Incident object set, and all object and link types use Object Storage v2. Its table shows incident properties and a column with the assigned Crew's status from a linked object. Incident changes appear within seconds, but crew status changes appear only after a manual reload. Crew status must refresh automatically, with the least extra data load. Which change should the builder make?

choices.text: Also watch the Crew object set through a simple widget in a zero-size section, since linked object types are not watched automatically
Add a Refresh data in module button that dispatchers press whenever they suspect that crew information in the table is out of date
Lower the minimum seconds between refreshes to 10, so the module reloads incidents together with their linked crews more often than now
Show crew status inside an embedded child module that has auto-refresh configured on Crew objects, placed in the incident table's section

stem: An inspection module lets users save states that include the inspection selected in an Object Dropdown widget, whose output variable has an external ID used for state saving. The team now wants an Object Selection widget so users can pick several inspections. Hundreds of saved states exist and must keep reloading correctly, and users must not have to save their states again. What should the builder do?

choices.text: Replace the widget and give its output variable the same external ID as the old variable, so existing saved states load into it
Replace the widget and let Workshop give its new output variable a fresh external ID, since saved states store variables under their display names
Replace the widget and mark one of the old saved states as the module's default state, so it applies automatically for every user
Keep the Object Dropdown and add an Object Selection widget beside it, asking users to move to new saved states gradually over time

stem: A developer registers a confidential client for an internal OSDK web application, configures a redirect URL, and stores the client secret in the server's vault. When test users from the developer's own Organization start the authorization code flow, they cannot authorize the application. The application must act with each user's own permissions, and the security team wants project and marking restrictions on what it can reach. What step is missing?

choices.text: Send the redirect URL again in the token request body, because the authorization step ignores the redirect URLs set at registration
Enable the application for the users' Organization, which is also where its project access and marking restrictions are configured
Switch the application to the client credentials grant, so that test users no longer need an authorization step before using it
Rotate the client secret, because a secret stored outside the registration page cannot be used during the user authorization step

stem: A reporting service runs at 02:00 and builds each analyst's personal report from Foundry using exactly the data that analyst may see. Analysts are not signed in at that hour, auditors require every read to be attributed to the analyst it serves, and the service runs on a secured server that can hold client secrets. Which authentication design meets these requirements?

choices.text: The client credentials grant, giving the service user access to every analyst's data and filtering each report in the service's own code
The authorization code grant without offline_access, asking every analyst to sign in to the service again each evening before 02:00
A personal token of one administrator for every report, with the service filtering each report by that analyst's group memberships
The authorization code grant with offline_access, storing each analyst's refresh token securely and refreshing tokens at run time

stem: A fleet application built with the OSDK, with a backend service that can hold credentials, shows Vehicles and Charging Stations. Each user may see only the Vehicles their own Foundry permissions allow, but every user must see all Charging Stations without being granted access to the station data, and no copy of station data may leave Foundry. Which Developer Console permission setup fits?

choices.text: User permissions only, granting every application user Viewer access on the Charging Station data so that all stations become visible
Application permissions only, giving the service user access to Vehicles and stations and filtering vehicles per user in the backend code
Both types: user permissions for reading Vehicles, and application permissions through the service user for reading Charging Stations
User permissions only, exporting Charging Stations nightly to a file served by the application's own web server for every user to read

stem: An OSDK application that reads Shipment objects with user permissions worked for months. After the data team configured a new backing dataset for the Shipment object type, users get permission errors in the application, although they have full access to the new dataset and still see shipments in Workshop. No application code or SDK version changed. What should the developer do first?

choices.text: Grant the affected users the Editor role on the project with the new dataset, since read access is not enough for applications
Update the application's resource access scope in Developer Console to include the new backing dataset flagged as stale
Switch the application to application permissions, so its service user reads Shipment objects regardless of what each user can access
Generate a new SDK version and redeploy the application, because the generated Shipment type no longer matches the Ontology definition

stem: A team ships a mobile OSDK application whose users install updates on their own schedule, often weeks late. The next SDK version removes the deprecated Legacy Order object type. Older application versions still read Legacy Order and must keep working until their users upgrade, and the security team wants the application's access to Legacy Order removed once no version needs it. What is the best plan?

choices.text: Keep Legacy Order in the SDK and in the resource access scope permanently, so that no version of the application can break because of it
Register a second application for the new version and leave the old application with Legacy Order in its scope for as long as it exists
Remove Legacy Order from both the SDK and the resource access scope in the same release, since the new version no longer uses it
Remove Legacy Order from the SDK but keep it in the resource access scope until all clients upgrade, then clean it out of the scope

stem: An automation watches Support Ticket objects added to an Escalated set and runs a Bulk Assign Action that takes a set of tickets and assumes they all share one Category. Bursts of escalations across several categories arrive together. Each category's tickets in a burst must reach the Action in one run that holds only that category, and the team will not maintain one automation per category. Which execution mode fits?

choices.text: Execute once for each batch of objects with a batch size of one, so that every Bulk Assign run receives exactly one ticket
Execute once for all objects, so a single Bulk Assign run receives every ticket that was escalated in the same burst of activity
Execute once for each group of objects, grouping by the Category property of the tickets that triggered the condition
One automation per category, each with an object set filtered to its Category and the Execute once for all objects mode

stem: An automation's Action effect writes approved orders to a partner system through a webhook, a few hundred objects per night. The partner has planned outages of up to four hours, short rate-limit errors also occur, and objects that still fail after an outage must land in a manual-review queue. Nobody should have to retry events by hand after an outage. Which retry configuration fits best?

choices.text: Effect retries with backoff for rate limits, event retries every two hours up to three times, and a fallback to the review queue
Event retries every two hours up to three times, with no fallback, and the team checking failed events in the history every morning
Event retries every 30 minutes up to five times, with a fallback effect that sends objects still failing to the review queue
Effect retries with exponential backoff and jitter only, set with a long maximum delay so that the attempts stretch across the outage

stem: A maintenance team assigns Work Orders to regions, and planners often move orders between regions during the day. An automation must notify a regional lead whenever the priority of an open Work Order in Region North changes. It must not fire when a work order merely moves into Region North, nor when any other property changes, and it should react within minutes of an edit. Which condition configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Objects modified in set on open North work orders, watching only the priority property, with include objects added enabled for new arrivals
Objects added to set on North work orders filtered to the new priority value, evaluated by a scheduled check once every hour
Objects modified in set on open North work orders, watching only the priority property, with include objects added and removed disabled
Objects modified in set on open North work orders with no properties selected, so any change to an order in the set triggers it

stem: A finance team automates its invoice process with two existing Actions. When an Invoice becomes Approved, an automation must apply Reserve Funds first and Notify Vendor second. Notify Vendor must never run for an invoice whose reservation failed, even when a fallback effect handles that failure, and approvals arrive in batches of up to 40 invoices. How should the effects be configured?

choices.text: Two separate Action effects set to execute sequentially, with Reserve Funds as the first effect and Notify Vendor as the second
One Action effect with both Actions configured inside it, Reserve Funds listed first, so they run in the order in which they are listed
A Notification effect for the vendor and an Action effect for Reserve Funds, with the two effects set to execute sequentially
Two Action effects set to execute in parallel, with a fallback on Reserve Funds that cancels the vendor notice after a failure

stem: An automation that updates Shipment objects from carrier events failed for 120 events overnight because its Action referenced a property the ontology team had renamed. The developer paused the automation and fixed the Action's configuration. Now exactly the failed events must be processed, without waiting for new triggers, and live triggers must not fire until the team has verified the fix. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Unpause the automation and let the failed events retry by themselves at the next evaluation of the automation's condition
Unpause first and then retry the failed events, since retries are blocked on paused automations until live triggers resume
Let the automation expire, copy it with the fixed Action, and manually run the copy over every object in the monitored set
Keep the automation paused and retry the failed events, which reruns the selected effects using the latest configuration

stem: An AIP Logic function classifies a maintenance request and uses an Apply action block to set the request's Priority. Called from a Workshop function-backed variable, it returns the right classification, yet Priority never changes on the object. The edit must be applied only when a planner confirms it, and the Logic function must stay the single place where classification happens. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Replace the Apply action block with a Use LLM block that has the Apply actions tool, so that the model itself applies the Priority edit
Back an action type with the Logic function and have the planner's confirm button in Workshop apply that action to the request
Copy the classification prompt into a TypeScript function-backed Action and keep the Logic function only for display in Workshop
Call the Logic function from an automation with a Logic effect whenever a request is created, so that edits are applied straight away

stem: An AIP Logic function drafts replies to customer complaints. Its Use LLM block uses the Query objects tool on Order objects that have 60 properties, and the Debugger's token bar turns red on long cases. The reply needs only order date, status and delivery address, the team wants predictable output, and the security team rejects sending unused personal fields to the model. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Switch the block to a model with a larger context window, so that all 60 properties of every order fit into the prompt without errors
Limit the Query objects tool to order date, status and delivery address, and move other steps into deterministic blocks
Raise the temperature in the block's configuration so that the model writes shorter replies that consume fewer tokens per case
Split the work into three Use LLM blocks, each receiving all 60 properties for one third of the orders that relate to the complaint

stem: A team has two candidate functions for extracting contract renewal dates: an AIP Logic function and a TypeScript v2 function using regular expressions. They must compare both on the same 300 real Contract objects plus 20 hand-written edge cases, keep one set of test cases to maintain, measure exact date matches, and repeat the comparison after every prompt change. Which AIP Evals setup fits?

choices.text: One suite built only from the 300 object set test cases, with both functions as targets and an exact-match evaluator for each one
Two evaluation suites, one per function, each holding its own copy of the 300 contracts and the 20 hand-written edge-case test cases
One suite with both functions as target functions and an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator asking whether each returned date looks plausible
One suite with object set and manual test cases, both functions as target functions, and an exact date evaluator for each target

stem: An AIP Logic function summarizes every inspection report of a site in one Use LLM block. It finishes in about seven minutes in the Debugger, but fails each time a Workshop button calls it. It must stay callable from Workshop and from the function execution API, and the summary quality must not drop. What explains the failure, and what should change?

choices.text: The Debugger skips the five-minute limit enforced in Workshop and the API; restructure the work so a call ends within five minutes
Workshop runs Logic functions project-scoped, which blocks model calls; switch the function to user-scoped execution so the call succeeds
Workshop calls functions with a smaller token limit than the Debugger; switch the block to a 32k-context model so the request fits
Workshop calls the published version while the Debugger runs the draft, so republishing the latest draft will make the failure disappear

stem: A developer uses AI FDE to refactor a function repository. The team wants AI FDE to iterate on file edits and builds without a confirmation prompt at every step, any change on the protected main branch must still need explicit approval, and nothing may run under an identity other than the developer's own. How should the developer work with AI FDE?

choices.text: Give AI FDE a dedicated service account with edit rights on main, so that its changes are not held up by any approval prompts
Run the session on main and approve file edits for the whole session in advance, so that confirmation prompts stop appearing
Run the session on a feature branch, where file edits and builds auto-approve, and review the result before it is merged
Run the session on a feature branch and have AI FDE publish and tag the release itself, since publishing auto-approves there

stem: Patient objects are protected by an object security policy so that clinicians see only their own ward's patients. A new rule says that datasets derived from patient data, Workshop exports and Function outputs must also stay restricted to staff cleared for patient data, and engineers building downstream pipelines must not be able to bypass this. Which control should be added?

choices.text: A separate project for the derived datasets, with Viewer roles limited to cleared staff and no other roles granted to anyone else
A patient-data marking on the backing dataset, because markings propagate through derivation while policies only filter reads
Property security policies on every sensitive Patient property, so that derived datasets and exports inherit the column restrictions
A restricted view with the same ward rule in place of the object security policy, so that its filter follows the data downstream

stem: A new planner can open a Workshop module and switch between its pages, but its object table is empty and the Assign Crew button reports missing permissions. Colleagues with the same role on the module see data and can assign crews. Only what this workflow needs may be granted, and the module's owner does not know which data resources it depends on. What should the owner do first?

choices.text: Use the Check access panel on the module to list the planner's unmet data requirements on object, link and action types
Grant the planner Viewer on every project in the Ontology, so whichever data source the module uses becomes visible at once
Give the planner the Editor role on the Workshop module, since editing rights on a module also unlock its data and its Actions
Ask the planner to use Object Explorer for this work instead, since Workshop hides data from users who lack an Editor module role

stem: An automation owned by a service user of a third-party application updates overdue Contract objects each night and processes about 900 of them. After an outage, an analyst who can see contracts of only two regions starts a manual execution to catch up, and it processes just 310 contracts without any errors. The team needs to understand the gap before relying on manual runs. What explains it?

choices.text: Manual executions cap each run at one batch of the default size, and the remaining contracts wait for the next scheduled evaluation
The manual run applied the automation's notification permissions, so contracts with no eligible notification recipient were skipped
The manual run evaluated its input object set with the analyst's permissions, so only contracts the analyst can see were included
Manual executions only process objects added since the last scheduled run, so contracts handled before the outage were excluded

stem: A Supplier object type must stay visible to all procurement staff, but its Bank Account and Tax Number properties must be visible only to members of a Finance group, and the Supplier ID primary key must stay readable by everyone who can see the supplier. The team wants this enforced in the Ontology and will not maintain a second object type. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: A restricted view on the backing dataset that filters Supplier rows down to Finance group members whenever bank data is present
A second Supplier Banking object type holding Bank Account and Tax Number, linked one-to-one and visible only to Finance
An object security policy for procurement staff, plus a property security policy on Supplier ID, Bank Account and Tax Number requiring Finance
An object security policy for procurement staff, plus one property security policy on Bank Account and Tax Number requiring Finance

stem: A shared TypeScript Function used by four Workshop applications owned by different teams fails intermittently, a few times a day, with no clear pattern and no error shown to users beyond a generic message. The application developer must find the recurring error messages produced by that Function, see which applications depend on it, and avoid asking each application team for screenshots or reproduction steps. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Open Data Lineage for the Function's input datasets and check their build history for failed transactions around each incident
Run the Function repeatedly in the functions helper with sample inputs in Authoring until the failure shows up in the console
Open the Function in Workflow Lineage, search its service logs for recurring errors, and review its dependent applications
Add a notification rule to every Action in the four applications so that users report each failure together with its context

stem: An ontology developer links Project and Engineer with a many-to-many Staffed On link type backed by the join table dataset `project_engineer_pairs`, which holds project_id and engineer_id. A second team now needs a Reviewed By many-to-many link type between the same two object types for code reviews, and today its pairs happen to match the staffing pairs exactly. Saving Reviewed By on the same join table fails with `Phonograph2:DatasetAndBranchAlreadyRegistered`. Both link types must be editable through Actions independently of each other, review pairs will diverge from staffing pairs next quarter, and the developer has no access to change the staffing pipeline. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Keep only Staffed On and record reviews as a property on its links, so that one link type stored in `project_engineer_pairs` serves both teams
Back Reviewed By with its own join table dataset, for example one generated from the two primary keys, giving each link type separate editable data
Back Reviewed By with `project_engineer_pairs` after adding a link_kind column to it, so one datasource tells staffing pairs and review pairs apart
Back Reviewed By with a pipeline output that copies every row of `project_engineer_pairs`, so each link type has a separate datasource with today's pairs

stem: A facilities team built an automation with an Objects removed from set condition on Open Work Orders, defined as Work Order objects with status Open, and a notification effect to the site manager. Managers are told when an order moves to Closed or Cancelled. However, when a supervisor uses the Delete Work Order action on an open order created in error, no notification arrives and no event appears in the automation's history. Managers must hear about every deleted open order with its title, the team will not add object types, and deletions must stay real deletions because downstream reports count live objects. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Add a notification rule to the Delete Work Order action, addressed to the site manager, with content generated from the order before deletion
Add a notification rule to the Delete Work Order action, addressed to the supervisor who submits the deletion instead of the site manager
Change the automation's condition to Objects modified in set on Open Work Orders with include objects removed enabled, so that deletions count as removals
Change the automation to scheduled monitoring every 15 minutes, so that open orders that were deleted are found as removals at the next check

stem: An action type Create Shipment must create a Shipment object and link it to one or more existing Order objects through the many-to-many Contains link type in one submission. The developer configured a Create object rule for Shipment with an automatically generated primary key, then a Create link(s) rule meant to link the new shipment to an Order list parameter. The link rule offers only object reference parameters, so it cannot point at the shipment being created. Planners must keep a single form and submission, the team does not want to maintain function code, and the shipment's primary key must stay generated. What should the developer configure?

choices.text: Keep both rules but split them into two action types, Create Shipment and Link Orders, applied one after the other from one Workshop button
Replace both rules with a function rule whose Ontology edit function creates the shipment and adds the Contains links to each order
Keep both rules but change the Shipment rule to Create or modify object(s), so the link rule can reference the shipment by its generated key
Keep the Create object rule for Shipment and configure the Contains link to the Order list inside it, removing the Create link(s) rule

stem: A Close Incident action has worked for months for the operations group, whose members can view Incident objects and pass the criterion requiring the Operations group. Last week the ontology owner enabled an action log on the action type for an audit request. Since then operators' submissions fail at submission time with a permissions error, while the ontology owner, who has broad Ontology permissions, can still close incidents. Parameters, rules and submission criteria are unchanged. The action log must stay, operators must not gain access to any other object type, and the criteria must not change. What should be done?

choices.text: Give the operations group the permissions it needs on the action log's object type, as submitters need them for each type the action creates
Give the operations group the permissions it needs on the action log's object type, and remove the Operations criterion so the log can be written
Give the operations group a role on the action type itself, because enabling an action log adds a separate permission check on the type
Give the operations group Edit on Incident's writeback dataset, because enabling an action log reopens Incident to edits beyond Actions

stem: A Ticket object type is backed by a dataset with a `last_synced_at` timestamp column in UTC, and its datasource uses the Apply most recent value conflict resolution strategy. An agent changes ticket 4411's priority to P0 through an action at 10:15 UTC, but the object still shows P2. The source row for 4411 has last_synced_at of 11:00 UTC the same day, because an upstream job stamps the end of its processing window instead of the actual update time. Edits to the edit-only Team property apply normally. Agents' edits must win whenever they are newer than the real source update, the strategy must stay, and source updates to priority must keep flowing. What is the cause and fix?

choices.text: The edit is older than the datasource timestamp, so it is ignored; add an action that sets last_synced_at to the edit time with each change
The edit is older than the datasource timestamp, so it is ignored; convert Priority to an edit-only property so that agents' edits always apply
The edit is older than the datasource timestamp, so it is ignored; change the pipeline so last_synced_at holds the actual source update time
The strategy needs a date column rather than a timestamp, so the edit is ignored; cast last_synced_at to a date in the upstream pipeline

stem: A TypeScript v1 edit function backs an Update Asset action. Its optional parameter `replacementTags?: string[]` is documented as "leave tags unchanged when omitted; otherwise replace tags with the list". Unit tests in the repository omit the parameter and pass. In production, whenever a user submits the action without touching the tags field, the asset's tags are wiped, and logs show the function received an empty array. Clearing all tags is done through a separate Clear Tags action, users who skip the field must still be able to submit, and the action must keep a single form. What should the developer change in the function?

choices.text: Treat an undefined or null replacementTags as no change, because actions send omitted optional arrays as null rather than as undefined
Treat an empty replacementTags array as no change, because actions pass omitted optional arrays as empty arrays rather than undefined
Treat only undefined replacementTags as no change, and add a unit test that passes an empty array to confirm that tags are kept
Treat an empty replacementTags array as no change, and add a submission criterion that also blocks an empty list from being submitted

stem: A Python edit function `assign_reviewers` adds Reviewer objects to a Document's many-to-many link whose API name is `assignedReviewers`; in code it is reached as `editable_doc.assigned_reviewers`. The decorator is `@function(edits=[Document, Reviewer])`. The function-backed action works in the source enrollment. When the team packages the function and action into a Marketplace product for another enrollment, the product does not list the link type as a dependency, and the reviewer links are missing after installation. The function must stay in Python, the team will keep one action, and provenance must be fixed in the function itself. What should change?

choices.text: Add `OntologyLinkType(Reviewer, "assignedReviewers")` to the decorator's edits list, naming the object type on the far side of the link
Add `OntologyLinkType(Document, "assigned_reviewers")` to the decorator's edits list, matching the snake_case attribute used in the code
Remove Reviewer from the decorator's edits list and keep only Document, since link edits are recorded against the object type that holds them
Add `OntologyLinkType(Document, "assignedReviewers")` to the decorator's edits list, using the source object type and the link's API name

stem: A sales-operations team published a TypeScript v2 edit function at version 0.4.0 and backs a Score Lead action with it. They want the action to follow compatible fixes automatically, but the auto upgrade option is unavailable on the action's function rule. After they publish 0.4.1 with a bug fix, the action still runs 0.4.0. The function's API is now stable, production use starts next week, the action must not need an edit for every patch release, and breaking changes must never reach the action unreviewed. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Publish the stable API as 1.0.0, select 1.0.0 as the minimum version, and turn on auto upgrade for compatible releases on the action
Publish the stable API as 0.5.0 and turn on auto upgrade, because only versions below 0.5.0 are reserved for initial development
Keep publishing 0.y.z versions and turn on auto upgrade from 0.4.1, because patch releases inside 0.4 are treated as backward compatible
Publish the stable API as 1.0.0 and keep the action pinned, upgrading its function rule by hand after each patch release is published

stem: A control-room module watches an Alarm object set with auto-refresh, and all object and link types are on Object Storage v2. The watched set is defined with a phrase filter on the alarm description typed by the operator, and it feeds a table in a drawer that operators open during incidents. Even while the drawer is open during an incident, alarm changes never refresh the table, although other watched sets in the module refresh normally. The minimum seconds between refreshes is already 10. Operators must see changes while the drawer is open, and the typed phrase filter must remain. What should the builder change?

choices.text: Watch the same phrase-filtered Alarm object set, and add a Refresh data in module event to the button that opens the drawer during incidents
Watch an unfiltered Alarm object set for auto-refresh, and apply the operator's phrase filter in a separate variable derived from it
Watch an unfiltered Alarm object set for auto-refresh, and remove the phrase filter from the table so operators scroll through every alarm instead
Watch the same phrase-filtered Alarm object set, and move the table from the drawer onto the main page so that the watched set is always visible

stem: A module uses a string variable `activePage` for variable-backed page selection, and a header widget shows a breadcrumb computed from `activePage`. A button on the Overview page runs two events: Switch to Details page, then Set variable value copying the selected order into `focusOrder`. The Details page opens correctly and `focusOrder` is set, but the breadcrumb still says Overview, and a function-backed variable using `activePage` keeps computing Overview metrics. Navigation must stay a single click, the page structure must stay as it is, and the breadcrumb must always match the visible page. What should the builder change?

choices.text: Keep both events but move Switch to Details page after Set variable value, so that activePage is updated as the last step of the click
Keep both events and add a Recompute event for the breadcrumb after Switch to Details page, so the header picks up the new page
Convert the pages into tabs of a Tabs layout backed by activePage, since switching tabs does update the backing string variable
Replace Switch to Details page with a Set variable value event that sets activePage to Details, keeping the copy into focusOrder

stem: A confidential OSDK backend acts for users through the authorization code grant with offline_access. Two identical worker instances share a database row holding each user's refresh token. Both may refresh when an access token expires, and whichever finishes last writes its new refresh token to the row. For days everything worked, but now some users must sign in again every morning. Logs show one instance presenting a refresh token that the other instance had already used three minutes earlier, followed by every token from that user's grant being rejected. The team must keep two instances, must keep acting for users, and must not ask users to sign in daily. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Let both instances refresh freely but make them refresh within one minute of each other, since reuse inside one minute is allowed
Let both instances refresh freely but always write back the original refresh token from sign-in, so that both always hold the same value
Let only one instance refresh a user's token at a time using a lock, and store each newly rotated refresh token before it is used
Switch both instances to the client credentials grant, so that no user refresh tokens have to be shared between the two instances

stem: A native desktop app registered as a public client sends users to the authorization endpoint with a code_challenge using S256. To limit load, its sign-in helper queues returned authorization codes and exchanges them at the token endpoint in batches every 15 minutes, sending client_id, code, redirect_uri and the matching code_verifier. Users who sign in just before a batch run succeed, while those who sign in shortly after one get an error and must sign in again. The app cannot hold a client secret, PKCE must stay, and users must not have to sign in twice. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Exchange each authorization code at the token endpoint as soon as the redirect arrives, because codes expire 10 minutes after issue
Keep the 15-minute batches and drop code_verifier from the token request, because verifying it is what fails for codes held longer
Keep the 15-minute batches and request the offline_access scope, so that queued authorization codes are accepted for a longer time
Keep the 15-minute batches and add the client secret to each token request, because delayed exchanges need a confidential client's secret

stem: A logistics team's Developer Console application has three members: Mina, the employee who created it and holds Owner, Jae, an employee who holds Editor, and a contractor who also holds Editor. Mina starts four weeks of leave tomorrow. A new employee, Arjun, must add object types to the application's SDK and generate new SDK versions during that time. When Jae tries to share the application with Arjun, he cannot, although Jae himself still adds entities and generates SDK versions without trouble. Policy says the contractor must never be able to share the application, at least one employee must be able to grant access while Mina is away, and nobody may create new Developer Console applications without approval. What should be done today?

choices.text: Mina gives Arjun the Viewer role before she leaves, because Viewer lets him add object types and generate new SDK versions of the application
Mina gives Jae the Third-party application administrator role, because sharing an existing application needs the role that creates applications
Mina gives the contractor the Owner role for one day so she can share the application with Arjun, and then sets her back to Editor
Mina gives Jae the Owner role on the application, so Jae can share it with Arjun as Editor while the contractor keeps her Editor role

stem: An automation triggers when Purchase Line objects are added to a Pending set and runs a Logic effect once per object; each Logic run also updates the parent Purchase Order's running total. Bursts of 60 lines from one order arrive together. Run history shows many failures with `Actions:ObjectVersionChanged`, almost all in such bursts, while single-line orders never fail. Parallelization is at its default and no event retry strategy is configured. Totals must end up correct, longer runtimes are acceptable, and the Logic function cannot be redesigned this sprint. Which change addresses the evidence best?

choices.text: Keep the default parallelization of 20 and replace the Logic effect with a function effect that returns the same Ontology edits
Lower the Logic effect's custom parallelization below the default of 20 and add an event retry strategy, as this error is retryable
Raise the Logic effect's custom parallelization above the default of 20 and add an event retry strategy, so bursts finish sooner
Keep the default parallelization of 20 and switch the condition to scheduled monitoring, so a burst is combined into one trigger event

stem: A logistics automation uses an Objects added to set condition on Delayed Shipments, defined as Shipment objects with status Delayed, a single object type with no derived-property filters and no function-generated set. Shipment is fed by a batch pipeline. Last month the Shipment object type was migrated from Object Storage v1 to v2 so that the automation could use live monitoring, yet it still evaluates on its hourly schedule and customers hear of delays up to an hour late. Nobody has edited the automation since before the migration. Compute cost must not grow, and the condition logic must stay the same. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Move the Shipment feed to a streaming pipeline, because live monitoring of added objects needs stream-backed object types
Shorten the automation's schedule to every minute, because Objects added to set conditions support only scheduled monitoring
Re-save the automation, so that it picks up the Object Storage v2 backing of Shipment and can switch to live monitoring
Rebuild the condition on a function that returns delayed shipments as an object set, a source that supports live monitoring

stem: An automation sends a notification to a dynamic list of recipients, the account owners linked to each Opportunity that enters a Closing Soon set. Most owners are notified, but newly hired owners receive nothing and see no activity on the automation. Access checks show the new hires have Viewer on the Opportunity objects and all their properties, and the object type has a single datasource. The automation sits in a project where new hires hold no role. Notifications must reach every linked owner, new hires must not see the project's other automations, and the automation owner must not change. What should be done?

choices.text: Give the new hires Viewer on this automation itself, which recipients need in addition to Viewer on the triggering objects
Give the new hires Viewer on the Opportunity backing dataset, because notifications check the datasource rather than the objects
Move the automation to third-party application ownership, so that notifications are sent with the service user's permissions instead
Give the new hires Editor on the project containing the automation, so they meet the project role that notification recipients need

stem: A support team runs an AIP Logic function used by 200 agents in user-scoped execution, the default. When an agent reports a bad recommendation two days later, the support engineer cannot find that run: she sees only her own executions, and the agent's logs have expired. Recommendations do not depend on which agent runs the function, all resources it uses are already imported into its project, and support engineers hold the markings on them. The team wants every engineer to see all runs and a durable record of recent runs for analysis. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Switch to project-scoped execution and rely on its execution logs alone, without configuring a run history dataset for analysis
Keep user-scoped execution and give support engineers the Owner role on the project, so they can open every user's execution logs
Keep user-scoped execution and configure a run history dataset, so that every agent's run is written as a row for later analysis
Switch to project-scoped execution and configure a run history dataset, which logs each run as a row and keeps the latest 10,000

stem: Team managers run an AIP Logic function, through an action, that reads Performance Review objects with the Query objects tool and writes a short Team Health summary to a property of the Team object. Performance Review objects are protected by an object security policy that lets each manager read only their own team's reviews, and access checks confirm that ordinary staff cannot see any review. Yet staff, who can view Team objects, now read sentences quoting individual reviews in the summaries. Summaries must stay on the Team object, managers must keep generating them with the same function, and staff must keep seeing every other Team property. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Run the function in project-scoped mode, so that its reads and writes no longer depend on the permissions of the manager who runs it
Protect the summary property with a property security policy that applies the review policy's manager rule, so only those managers read it
Limit the Query objects tool to fewer Performance Review properties, so that the model receives less review text when it writes each summary
Keep the review policy as it is, since object security policies on source objects also filter the outputs derived from them later on

stem: A Vendor object type is secured with an object security policy and materialized to a Foundry dataset that a finance pipeline reads. On Monday the ontology owner added a Sanctions marking to the object security policy. On Wednesday an auditor finds that users without the Sanctions marking can still read the materialized dataset's transactions from last week and from Tuesday. The materialization builds weekly on Sundays. Historical and new data in the materialized dataset must be protected today, the policy must stay on the object type, and the finance pipeline must keep reading the materialized dataset. What should the owner do?

choices.text: Build the materialization now, because a transaction under the updated policy also secures every earlier transaction of the dataset
Remove the object security policy and rebuild, so the materialized dataset falls back to the markings of the backing data sources
Build the materialization now and also apply the Sanctions marking to the materialized dataset, securing earlier transactions
Add the Sanctions marking to a property security policy as well, so that sensitive properties are hidden in the materialized rows

stem: A team configured an object security policy on a Contractor object type so that site managers see contractors assigned to their sites without access to the backing dataset, which also holds rates for every site. After saving, site managers still see no Contractor objects in Workshop, while users holding Viewer on the backing dataset see contractors correctly filtered by the policy. The enrollment still uses the legacy datasource-derived permissions model. Managers must not gain access to the backing dataset, and the team will keep object security policies for their fast policy updates. What should be done?

choices.text: Remove the markings inherited by the object security policy, so that managers without those markings can view the Contractor objects
Grant site managers Viewer on the backing dataset, so that the object security policy then filters which contractors each manager can see
Move the site rule into a restricted view on the backing dataset, and back the Contractor object type with that restricted view instead
Migrate the enrollment to project-based permissions, so that users no longer need Viewer on the backing data source to see the objects
